finding.claim: The caller's identity is read straight from the client-supplied HTTP header `X-Session-User-Verified`. The app does no session, signature or token verification. Any client who can reach the app can send the header with the name of a user who holds grants, and the app treats them as that user. That lets them delete or rename files they don't own. This is an authentication bypass and leads to broken authorization. It only holds if no trusted front proxy strips or overwrites this header. Nothing in this code does that.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request header `X-Session-User-Verified`, set to any victim or owner username.
finding.sink: `del STORE[fid]` in delete_file and `f["name"] = ...` in rename_file, both gated only by an ACL check on the spoofed identity.

trace.note: before_request copies the raw header value into g.user with no verification
is_allowed looks up resource['grants'][user], so the spoofed name matches the real owner's grants
rename_file uses the same spoofed g.user with the 'write' check

finding.guards_checked: Read both files. There is no authentication decorator, session or signature check, and no code that strips the header from incoming requests. The ACL check in acl.py is sound but only as trustworthy as the user value it receives. A missing header gives g.user=None, which fails the grants lookup, so anonymous requests are denied. A forged header is not. I didn't check for an upstream proxy, since none is in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo; acl.py:4-10 ACL checks are sound and enforced (ensure_allowed aborts, is_allowed result tested at views.py:25), but they trust g.user. Missing header gives None, which is denied.
verdict.reason: Every trace line is accurate (views.py:11 copies the raw header into g.user, views.py:17 and 25 pass it to the ACL, views.py:18 and 27 are the effects). Whether it is exploitable depends on whether a trusted front proxy sets or strips `X-Session-User-Verified`, as the "Verified" in the header name suggests, and no proxy or deployment config is in the repo to settle that.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Trusted upstream identity middleware per the project facts. The header name `X-Session-User-Verified` implies a proxy sets it after verification. The ACL checks (acl.py:5, acl.py:9-10) are sound.
verdict_facts.reason: The trace is accurate (views.py:11 reads the header into g.user, views.py:17 and :25 gate on the ACL, acl.py:5 and :9-10 deny when the user has no grant). The project facts say request identity is populated by trusted upstream middleware, so the "verified" header is not attacker-controlled, and the finding itself depends on the unproven assumption that no proxy overwrites it.
